schema.title: UpdateCredentialsRequest
schema.description: Send only the fields you want to change. Omitted fields are left as they are and aren't validated. To change the password, rotate it instead.

UserName.description:
A new login name. The old name is released.

A name already in use returns `422`, and a reserved name returns `400`; either way nothing
changes. Credentials that already have a reserved name can still update their other fields.

Alias.description: The label shown in the dashboard. An empty string resets it to the login name.

Permission.description: What the credentials can do with files under their home and chroot directories. Ignored on the organization's default credentials, and on credentials that have or are getting virtual folders.

HomeDirectory.description: Where the credentials land after connecting. An empty string resets it to `/home/{UserName}`. Must start with a slash, not end with one, and not contain a variable such as `${...}`.

ChrootDirectory.description: The highest directory the credentials can reach. An empty string resets it to `/`.

HomeDirectoryDetails.description:
Replaces the virtual folders, up to 50, and removes `Permission`, since each folder has its own.

Send an empty list or `null` to switch back to a home directory. The credentials then need a
`Permission`: send one in the same request, or the request returns `400` unless they already
have one.

The organization's default credentials can't use virtual folders.

items.title: VirtualFolder
items.description: One virtual folder: a path the credentials see, mapped to a location in your storage, with its own permission.

Entry.description: The path the credentials see, such as `/inbound`. Must start with a slash and not end with one. The root `/` must be the only entry. Entries can't share a path, contain one another, or contain a variable such as `${...}`.

Target.description: The location in your storage, as a path from the root of your bucket. Must start with a slash and not end with one. Two entries can show the same location only with the same permission.

Type.description: Whether the entry is a folder or a single file. Defaults to `DIRECTORY`. A `FILE` entry can't be the root `/`.

Permission.description: What the credentials can do inside this entry, with the same levels as `Permission` on the credentials. `none` keeps the entry listed but denies everything in it.

Email.description: Where web portal invitations and password resets are sent. Changing it marks the address unverified. An empty string removes it.

State.description: Whether the credentials can connect. The activate and deactivate calls do the same and read more clearly.

ExpiresAt.description:
When access stops, in **Unix epoch seconds**, or `null` to remove the expiry. Must be after the end of today and at most a year away.

When the time passes, the credentials become `inactive` and `ExpiresAt` returns to `null`.

Settings.title: CredentialsSettingsInput
Settings.description: The settings you can change. Each part you send is merged into the current settings, and a list you send replaces the stored one.

MFA.description: Multi-factor authentication for web portal sign-in.

Required.description: Whether the person using these credentials must use a second factor from their next portal sign-in.

Network.description: Where these credentials may connect from.

InboundRules.description:
The complete list of inbound rules, up to 250. Replaces the current list.

Requires a plan that includes inbound rules. On other plans the list is left unchanged and
the request still succeeds.

items.title: InboundRule
items.description:
A network rule that allows connections to a set of credentials from an address or range.

A connection is allowed when any enabled `allow` rule matches its protocol and source address,
counting your organization's rules and the credentials' rules together. Rules on credentials can
only add to what the organization allows. New organizations start with one organization rule that
allows every address; tighten it before rules on credentials make a difference.

Id.description: An identifier you choose, unique within these credentials. The dashboard uses a UUID.

Protocol.description: The connections the rule applies to: `*` for every protocol, or `SFTP`, `FTPS` or `WEB_PORTAL`. Case-sensitive.

State.description: Whether the rule is in effect. A `disabled` rule is kept but never matches.

Action.description: What a matching connection may do. Only `allow` rules are evaluated.

Source.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range such as `203.0.113.0/24`.

Description.description: A note explaining why the rule exists. Shown in the dashboard.

homeDirectory.summary: Go back to a home directory

network.summary: Allow connections from one more range
